text: New York's subway started as a turf war. Three rival systems, one city.
In nineteen oh four, the IRT opened the first underground line. The city built it. A private company ran it.
Then came the BMT, another private operator, spreading across Brooklyn and Queens.
And in nineteen thirty two, the city launched its own competitor: the IND.
Three systems meant separate fares, duplicate routes, and lines that didn't connect. And a fixed nickel fare left the private companies struggling.
So in nineteen forty, the city bought out the IRT and BMT, and the three became one.
Free transfers came later. And in nineteen sixty eight, the state's new MTA took over.
Next up: the Interborough Express. A planned fourteen mile light rail line linking Brooklyn and Queens, along an existing freight corridor.
Eighteen stations, and no detour through Manhattan.
It's still in design and environmental review. No opening date yet.
Congrats! You just rode through more than a century of subway history.
